Topics.type1_consolidated:
## Appraisals
Students found several aspects of the Topics course praiseworthy. They appreciated the inclusion of new content, the quality of the material, and the engaging nature of the sessions and dialogues. The Python units and coding exercises were also highlighted positively. Additionally, the structured query language and tables were well-received, and the visual aids used for each topic were considered beneficial.

## Criticisms
Some students expressed concerns about the course content being outdated and not modern enough. They felt that the pace was slow and that the subjects lacked relevance to contemporary applications. The scripting sections were noted as difficult without sufficient walkthroughs or practical examples. Furthermore, derivations and justifications were seen as overly lengthy and not contributing effectively to the learning process.

## Suggestions
Improvements suggested by students include the addition of more hands-on labs and practical examples, especially in Python programming. There was a call for clearer and more organized presentations, with a reduction in the length of derivations and justifications. Some students recommended incorporating more recent algorithms and NLP applications into the course material to make it more engaging and relevant.
Topics.type2_positive: Students found several aspects of the Topics course praiseworthy, with a particular emphasis on the new and engaging content, the quality of the material and sessions, and the effectiveness of the teaching methods. They appreciated the structured approach to the syllabus and the logical arrangement of the program. The coding sections, especially those involving Python, were highlighted as beneficial and well-delivered. Additionally, students commended the use of visuals and real-world examples like case studies and dialogues, which enhanced their understanding. The inclusion of novel subjects and the overall substance of the course were also noted positively, indicating that the course content was both comprehensive and engaging.
Topics.type3_negative: Students found the scripting aspect particularly challenging and suggested more Python examples from the instructor. They also criticized the excessive and seemingly unnecessary derivations, suggesting clearer and more concise presentations. Students felt that the course material was unengaging and outdated, with a need for more modern and relevant content. The justifications provided in the classes were perceived as overly lengthy and not worthwhile. Additionally, there was a call for more hands-on practice, including coding drills and practical sessions, to better understand the concepts. The overall structure of the course was seen as disorganized and slow-paced, with a desire for more organized and engaging sessions.

Organization.type1_consolidated:
## Appraisals
Students found the organization of classes well-arranged and beneficial, praising the structured class and homeworks. They appreciated the beautiful arrangement of sessions and the logical structure of the module. The lectures were noted for their good pacing and clarity, and the assignments were seen as tough yet useful. Additionally, team-based homework was highlighted for aiding mutual understanding.

## Criticisms
Students expressed dissatisfaction with the alignment between practicals and theoretical classes, noting that practicals were often more difficult than what was covered in lectures. There was concern about the rapid pace of the lectures and insufficient coverage of material. The timetabling was criticized for hampering rehearsal and causing confusion. The practical tasks were perceived as overly complex and not aligned with the theory, leading to significant stress for students. The lack of guidance and support during practical sessions was also a recurring complaint.

## Suggestions
Suggestions included increasing the exam duration to account for login issues, providing sample exercises and questions before practical sessions, and offering more support to novice students. Students recommended allowing students to choose their own teams to ease the challenge of working with unfamiliar peers. There was a call for better alignment between practicals and lectures, with some suggesting the inclusion of introductory materials in practical sessions. Some also proposed extending the duration of practicals and labs to accommodate the complexity of the tasks.
Organization.type2_positive: Students appreciated the well-organized and structured nature of the course, highlighting that the classes, lectures, and homeworks were effectively arranged to enhance learning. They noted that the homeworks were beneficial and built competencies, while the class sessions and exams were well-planned and paced appropriately. The overall organization, including the lecture schedule and study resources, was praised for its clarity and effectiveness in supporting their understanding and performance. Students also mentioned that the frequent assessments and logical structure of the module contributed significantly to their learning experience.
Organization.type3_negative: Students expressed significant dissatisfaction with the organization of the course, highlighting several key issues. They found that practical sessions did not align well with theoretical classes, making the practical tasks overly challenging and creating a sense of stress and inadequacy. Additionally, there was a perceived mismatch between the depth of material covered in lectures and the complexity of the practical assignments, leading to confusion and frustration. The structure of the course was also criticized for being poorly organized, with disjointed sessions that failed to build a coherent understanding of the subject matter. Furthermore, students felt that the grouping of unfamiliar peers and the lack of proper guidance during practical sessions added to the difficulty and stress. Overall, the organization of the course was seen as chaotic and unhelpful, hindering effective learning and causing considerable tension among students.
